# Working Notes: FY2025 NDAA — Preamble through Sec. 128

## Enactment / Naming Provisions

**Public Law 118-159**, 118th Congress; enacted Dec. 23, 2024; originated as H.R. 5009.
- Purpose: authorize FY2025 appropriations for DoD military activities, military construction, DOE defense activities; prescribe military personnel strengths.

**Sec. 1 — Short Title**
- Cited as "Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025."
- (b) Any reference to "National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025" in this/any other Act = reference to this Act. (10 USC 101 note.)

**Sec. 2 — Organization**
- 7 divisions: A (DoD Authorizations), B (Military Construction), C (DOE National Security), D (Funding Tables), E (Other Matters), F (Intelligence Authorization Act FY2025), G (Dept of State Authorization Act FY2025).

**Sec. 3 — Definitions**
- "this Act" in Divisions A–D = Divisions A–D only (1 USC 1 note).
- "congressional defense committees" per 10 USC 101(a)(16).

**Sec. 4 — Budgetary Effects**
- PAYGO effects (Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010) determined by latest "Budgetary Effects of PAYGO Legislation" statement, if submitted before House passage vote.

**Sec. 5 — Joint Explanatory Statement**
- JES printed in House section of Congressional Record ~Dec. 11, 2024; treated as if joint explanatory statement of conference committee.

## Division A, Title I — Procurement

**Sec. 101 — Authorization of Appropriations**
- Authorizes FY2025 procurement funds for Army, Navy/Marine Corps, Air Force/Space Force, Defense-wide, per funding table in Sec. 4101.

### Army Programs

**Sec. 111 — Centralized Security Monitoring Program (10 USC 7013 note)**
- Secretary of Army develops plan for Centralized Security Monitoring Program for Army installations/facilities in U.S.
- Plan elements: cost-effective scalable security solution; ≥3 installations as monitoring hubs (mix of large/extra-large per 2016 Provost Marshal General business case analysis; geographic diversity); full cost breakdown (capital, networking, O&M estimate, funding schedule across FYDP per 10 USC 221, cost-savings); viability analysis; list of needed authorities.
- Deadline: submit completed plan to Armed Services Committees by **Sept. 1, 2025**.
- Limitation: may not commence until Secretary certifies to congressional defense committees sufficient MILCON/operational appropriations programmed.
- Implementation deadline: **Jan. 1, 2027**; if certification not submitted by then, implement as soon as practicable after certification.

**Sec. 112 — Robotic Targets Pilot Program (10 USC 10101 note)**
- Secretary of Army incorporates moving robotic target systems into live fire training for select reserve/National Guard infantry units.
- Named "Lethality and Warfighting Enhancement Program."
- ≥3 installations. Objectives: increase lethality; demonstrate effect on small arms proficiency.
- Unit selection factors: past performance, readiness (emphasis on deploying units), deployment likel

# Working Notes: Sections 129–241

## Subtitle C (Navy Programs, cont.)

**SEC. 129 — Constellation-Class Frigate Funding Limitation**
- Bars FY2025 Navy funds for construction of a Constellation-class frigate beyond basic/functional design phase (per 10 USC 8669c) until SecDef submits certification.
- Certification (subsec. b): required upon designated technical authority's final approval of 95% of all basic and functional design drawings.

- SecDef must give GAO timely access to documents.

# Working Notes: NDAA FY2025, Part 3

## SEC. 242 — Biotechnology Roadmap (10 USC 4001 note)
- **Purpose:** Requires SecDef (w/ USD R&E, USD A&S, service secretaries) to submit biotech roadmap to congressional defense committees within **1 year** of enactment.
- **Elements (b):** strategic objectives; goals/milestones w/ timelines; review of goals in updates; dev needs/priorities; tech maturity assessment; funding sources (incl. FYDP per §221 title 10); RDT&E plan/timeline/metrics; rapid acquisition assessment; org roles (incl. Office of Strategic Capital, DARPA investment priorities); overall security risk; federal requirements hindering biotech; workforce dev; workforce specifics (positions now/5yr/10yr, filled positions, qualifications, challenges, workforce codes, outside expertise mechanisms, retraining assessment); international partnership collaboration (existing/new partnerships, challenges incl. co-investment limits, export controls).
- **Biennial updates (c):** at least every 2 years until sunset.
- **Form (d):** may be classified w/ unclassified executive summary.
- **Public (e):** unclassified version posted annually on public DoD website.
- **GAO (f):** evaluation + report within **180 days** of initial roadmap.
- **Definition (g):** "biotechnology" = application of science/tech to living organisms/parts/products/models to alter materials for knowledge/goods/services.
- **Sunset (h):** terminates **10 years** after enactment.

## SEC. 243 — Electromagnetic Spectrum Plan in International Fora (10 USC 113 note)
- SecDef (w/ DoD CIO) develops + begins implementing **5-year plan** within **60 days** for advancing US defense interests at international spectrum orgs (incl. World Radiocommunication Conferences prep process).
- **Elements:** personnel/resourcing; pre-coordination processes w/ domestic partners/industry; cooperation w/ foreign partners.
- **Briefing:** to SASC/HASC within **180 days**, incl. funded/unfunded resourcing.

## SEC. 244 — Quantum Information Science (QIS) Strategic Plan
- SecDef develops **5-year** strategic plan for QIS RDT&E, procurement, implementation across DoD/covered Armed Forces.
- **Elements:** ID QIS techs solving operational challenges; transition plans; continuous evaluation/development.
- **Report** within **1 year**: plan + assessment of budget balance across budget activity 1 (basic research), 2 (applied research), 3 (advanced tech dev) per DoD FMR (DOD 7000.14-R vol 2B ch5).
- Updates permitted at Secretary's discretion.
- **Covered Armed Force:** Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Space Force.

## SEC. 245 — Defense Science Board Study: Kwajalein Atoll
- USD R&E directs DSB within **30 days** to study feasibility/advisability of designating Ronald Reagan Ballistic Missile Defense Test Site (RTS) + USAG-KA as Major Range and Test Facility Base.
- **Elements:** split funding history; garrison infrastructure; test asset operability; interrelationships; MIT Lincoln Laboratory relationship; role in DoD missions.
- **Deadline:** study complete by **May 15, 2025**;

# Working Notes: Sections 739–862 (Health Care + Acquisition)

## SEC. 739 — Plan to improve access to safe pharmaceuticals
- **Purpose/mechanism:** SecDef, coordinating with Military Pharmaceutical and Medical Device Vulnerability Working Group (est. §716, NDAA FY2024, PL 118-31), develops plan to improve access to safe pharma products, eliminate/mitigate pharmacy supply chain risks.
- **Elements:** country-of-origin visibility/analytics; supplier engagement for unknown-origin APIs/key starting material; reduce reliance on high/very-high risk sources; transition to domestic or Trade Agreements Act (19 U.S.C. 2501 et seq.) compliant alternatives; validate domestic/compliant supply; assess feasibility of DoD-owned pharma manufacturing facility (construction, equipment, budget/schedule); identify needed authorities; interagency collaboration.
- **Deadline:** briefing to Armed Services Committees within **180 days** of enactment.

## SEC. 740 — Pilot: delegation of authority to approve reserve recruits with medical conditions
- **Mechanism:** SecDef implements pilot within **180 days**; Secretary concerned (per 10 USC 101(a)) may delegate to Commander, US Military Entrance Processing Command, authority to approve service medical waivers for reserve enlistment/appointment.
- **Medical consultation process:** required if delegated; provider seeks input if more specific guidance needed.
- **Conditions:** Secretary identifies **not more than 3** preexisting disqualifying conditions (under DoDI 6130.03) that regularly/automatically receive waivers.
- **Duration:** two years.
- **Reports:** briefing within 90 days of commencement (list of conditions); report within 90 days of conclusion (# waivers by condition, risk assessment, avg. days to adjudicate before/during, recommendation on permanence).

---

# TITLE VIII — Subtitle A: Acquisition Policy and Management

## SEC. 801 — Cost data guidelines
- Amends **10 USC 3227(b)**: strikes "$100,000,000," inserts "an amount described in section 3041(c)(1)."

## SEC. 802 — Limitation on options for cost contracts
- Adds **10 USC 3322(d)**: covered contract limits low-rate production lots for fixed-price options to **not more than one**.
- **Waiver:** service acquisition executive (or SecDef for joint programs) if in best interest of DoD; may not delegate below service acquisition executive level.
- Defs: "covered contract" = cost-reimbursement contract for development of a major system; "major system" per §3041.

## SEC. 803 — Unilateral definitization as final decision
- Amends **10 USC 3372(b)**: unilateral definitization by contracting officer treated as final decision under chapter 71, title 41; contractor may appeal to Armed Services Board of Contract Appeals or US Court of Federal Claims.

- **Rapid prototyping:** field demonstrable prototype + residual operational capability within 5 years of approved requirement.

# Working Notes: NDAA FY2025, Parts of Titles X–XIII

## SEC. 1087 — DoD Working Group on Multilateral AI Coordination (10 USC 301 note)
- **Purpose:** Develop/coordinate AI initiatives among US allies/partners.
- **Deadline:** Establish (or designate) working group ≤90 days after enactment.
- **Organization:** Sec. of Defense designates senior civilian/military head; establishes process to determine participating member countries.
- **Responsibilities:** compare AI tools/practices; identify interoperability solutions (intel sharing, battlespace awareness); shared RDT&E strategy; data management incl. multi-level security; test defense industrial base; expand innovation/procurement; other activities as Sec. determines.
- **Knowledge/tech data:** each member country controls its own data under its own export control laws; not subject to other members' jurisdiction.
- **Termination:** Sept. 30, 2028; Sec. may extend if in national security interest.
- **Definitions:** "battlespace awareness" per JP 1-02; "covered operational use" = government use in defense context.

- **Definitions (herd):** "fully constituted" = ≥4 caisson squads of 11 horses each, 14 caparison horses, 4 outreach horses; "trained" per MDW Commander; "certified" by MDW Commander w/ equine/vet experts.

## SEC. 7215 — Rest & Recuperation / Overseas Operations Leave
- Amends Chapter 9 of Foreign Service Act of 1980 (22 USC 4081 et seq.); inserts new §903a and §903b after §903.
- **§903a (22 USC 4083a) R&R Leave:** Secretary/agency head may grant up to **20 days paid leave per leave year** for rest/recuperation to employees in combat zone, high risk/high threat post, or location with significant security/operational challenges.
  - "High risk, high threat post" per §104 Omnibus Diplomatic Security Act (22 USC 4803).
  - Sole/exclusive discretion of agency head. Leave recorded separately.
- **§903b (22 USC 4083b) Overseas Operations Leave:** up to **10 days paid leave per leave year** to employees serving abroad for local holidays. Sole discretion of agency head.
- "Agency" excludes GAO; "employee" excludes uniformed services.
- Clerical amendment to table of contents (Public Law 96-465).

## SEC. 7216 — Overseas Crisis Response System (22 USC 4865 note)
- Secretary designates **Senior Focal Point for Crisis Management and Response** (reports directly to Secretary).
- **Tabletop exercises/simulations:** within **120 days** of enactment, then annually for 3 years; conducted in DC metro area.
- Briefing to Congress within **90 days** after each exercise; may be classified. After **3 years** from enactment, notification replaces briefing (within 90 days).
- FSI training: review crisis curricula; ambassadorial seminar/DCM course to include crisis management.
- **Clearinghouse:** within **180 days**, establish "Department of State Emergency Response Lessons Learned Clearinghouse."
- "International crisis" defined = situation requiring change to operating status of diplomatic facilities (departure/evacuation).

## TITLE LXXIII — Information Security & Cyber Diplomacy
- **7301:** Amends §9508(a)(1) DoS Auth Act 2022 (22 USC 10305)—Regional Technology Officer Program administered by Bureau for Cyberspace and Digital Policy.
- **7302 (22 USC 10308 note) Spyware protection:** Within **120 days**—issue standards; survey compromises over prior 2 years; report to Congress. Notification within **60 days** of serious compromise. Annual report for **5 years**. "Foreign commercial spyware" per §1102A National Security Act (50 USC 3232a).
- **7303:** Report within **90 days** on Bureau of Consular Affairs cloud adoption.
- **7304:** Within **180 days**, CIO should consider piloting ≥3 IT systems (passport renewal focus).
- **7305 (22 USC 2651a note):** Secure tech solutions for employee use.
